lesson.title: The Inductor's Magnetic Piggy Bank: Storing Energy, Spending None
lesson.summary: An inductor's current lags its voltage by 90 degrees, and that lag produces the same zero average power result as a capacitor, though the energy is stored magnetically rather than electrically.
lesson.body:
Inductive Reactance describes how an inductor resists changes in current, and just as with a capacitor, that opposition comes bundled with a 90 degree phase shift, but in the opposite direction. Where a capacitor's current leads its voltage, an inductor's current lags its voltage by 90 degrees, because the inductor generates a back EMF proportional to the rate of change of current, so the current itself always trails behind the voltage that is driving those changes.

Let the inductor current be i(t) = Im cos(wt). The voltage across it is v(t) = L di/dt = -Im w L sin(wt), which can be written as Vm sin(wt + 180 degrees), or more simply as Vm cos(wt + 90 degrees) with Vm = Im w L. The instantaneous power is p(t) = v(t) i(t), and carrying through the same trigonometric identity used for the capacitor gives p(t) = -(Vm Im / 2) sin(2wt). Once again there is no constant term, only a component oscillating at twice the source frequency that is positive half the time and negative half the time. The average over a full cycle is exactly zero.

Here is a worked example with real numbers. Let L = 50 mH and drive the inductor at w = 2000 rad/s with a current amplitude Im = 2 A. The inductive reactance is XL = wL = (2000)(0.05) = 100 ohms. The voltage amplitude is Vm = Im XL = (2)(100) = 200 V. The reactive power is Q = Vm Im / 2 = (200)(2)/2 = 200 VAR, again expressed in VAR rather than watts because it represents oscillating energy flow rather than dissipation, consistent with how Reactive Power is defined for any purely reactive element. In RMS terms, Vrms = 200/1.41421 = 141.42 V and Irms = 2/1.41421 = 1.4142 A, and Vrms times Irms gives (141.42)(1.4142) = 200 VAR, matching the peak based calculation and confirming the result is internally consistent.

As with the capacitor, it is worth stating plainly: an ideal inductor dissipates zero average power. During part of each cycle the source pushes energy into the inductor's magnetic field as current builds up, and during the next part of the cycle that stored magnetic energy flows back out as the current collapses. No heat is generated inside an ideal inductor, the energy simply oscillates between the source and the inductor's magnetic field, two round trips per source cycle since the power waveform completes two full oscillations for every one cycle of the driving voltage.

The mirror image relationship between capacitors and inductors is not a coincidence. Both are reactive elements that store energy rather than dissipate it, one electrically and one magnetically, and both produce a 90 degree phase shift between voltage and current, just in opposite directions. That opposite sign is exactly why capacitive reactance and inductive reactance can cancel each other in a series RLC circuit at resonance, a fact that only makes sense once you have seen, as here, that neither element ever actually consumes energy on average.
